newsitem.title: USA: While Dole ponders, Kemp hits Clinton on lapses.
newsitem.headline: While Dole ponders, Kemp hits Clinton on lapses.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is guilty of fear-mongering, arrogance of power and broken promises, Republican vice presidential nominee Jack Kemp said on Saturday in part of a chorus of attacks on Clinton.

Kemp's strongly worded comments came while Republican presidential nominee Dole was closeted with advisers to decide on strategy for the final three weeks of the campaign. Some want Dole to hit Clinton on the so-called character issue as the way to attract votes.
House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich, campaigning in Georgia, said Dole "should tell the truth" about Clinton.
"If the truth seems like a hard line, that explains a lot about the president," said Gingrich, who blistered Clinton with allegations of ethical lapses.

For its part, the Clinton campaign said Americans wanted a campaign of "issues, not insults." Campaign director Ann Lewis said Republicans tried to smear Clinton while disclaiming that was their intent.
Later in the day, Kemp said on CNN's "Evans & Novak" program there would be no personal attacks on Clinton but that he and Dole would point out Clinton's shortcomings.
"We are going to treat them with civility and bring out the lack of the high standard that they set for themselves," he said.
Kemp acknowledged "I lost" a televised debate with Vice President Al Gore if judged "on debating points but (I) won the debate on outlining Bob Dole's vision of the future."

Clinton has held the advantage in public opinion polls for weeks. The Reuter daily tracking poll showed Clinton with a 10-point lead on Saturday. Pollster John Zogby said the large lead for Clinton was giving a boost to Democrats running for Congress.
As part of the Republican response to the president's weekly radio speech, Kemp said Clinton had fallen woefully short of his promise of "the most ethical administration in history."

"But four years later, the words that seem to characterize the ethics of this administration are words like 'Travelgate', 'Filegate', independent counsels and possible presidential pardons," Kemp said.

"These problems add up to a pattern that is sad and troubling to all Americans -- Democrats, Republicans and independent. An arrogance of power. The avoidance of responsibility. For this administration, taking credit is everything and the truth is expendable."

Kemp's list of shortcomings included failure to enact a middle-class tax break, claiming "victory in the face of foreign policy failures," "demagoguery" about the future of Medicare and Medicaid (health insurance), improper dismissal of workers from the White House travel office and improperly gathering FBI files on Republicans who worked at the White House during the 1980s.

"We don't believe in disparaging anyone's personal character," Kemp said on the radio. "But we have a duty to talk about this administration's posturing and their public disregard for the very standards they set for themselves."
